traps.evidence: "what the problem was, what you changed, the team's result (12th of 68) stated plainly, not oversold" — attributed to the team, though the join date is not raised.
"mounting points, material callouts, the 18%-lighter number appearing as a dimension label" — figure printed unqualified, no CAD/simulation or not-yet-machined caveat.
"Framed honestly as a first-year group project: what the mechanism does, your part in it. No attempt to make it look bigger than it was."
"A short strip: what you fix, since when." No count of repairs appears anywhere in the first reply.
"No testimonials section — you were right to flag you don't have any, and a fake one would undercut everything else."

swap.reason: The teardown idea is anchored in her two actual artefacts — the pedal box bracket geometry and the 1984 frame stripped on the garage floor — plus her own job-card and logbook formats, so it would not transfer unchanged.

backdrop.reason: By the plan's own account the 3D carries no unique content — reduced motion and load failure both resolve to a static render where "the content never disappears, only the animation does."

depth.reason: The page is a ranked run of independent project sections (bracket, charger, co-op, restoration, skills, contact) whose order could be shuffled without breaking anything; the claimed strip-down-then-rebuild arc is never actually carried across the sections.

clipart.reason: The focal object is her own pedal box bracket geometry rather than a stock engineering emblem, though it is not held on screen throughout.

honesty.reason: Every contested item is correctly qualified in the final plan — team result dated before she joined, bracket tagged CAD-and-simulation only, charger as a group of four, no bike count, no testimonials.

thirty_seconds.reason: Hero gives name, course and the placement ask with a CV download, the at-a-glance strip gives correctly qualified proof, and the persistent bar anchors straight to contact.

plain_reader.reason: "Second-year Mechanical Engineering, Hallam... Looking for a summer 2026 placement" is plain enough for any reader and unembarrassing to an engineer.

judgement.summary: This is a single "Teardown" concept: a long-scroll page of conventional sections (hero, at-a-glance strip, two projects, co-op, restoration, skills, contact) dressed in technical-drawing language, with an exploded 3D bracket and a rotating gear train as its set pieces, and the co-op section borrowed from her own job-card format. Its greatest weakness is that the concept stays decorative — there is no through-line question, no persistent central object, and no order-dependent arc, so the 3D is an illustration the plan itself says can be swapped for a still without losing content.
